summary: Register gives a 1952 Georgia Forestry Commission tower in Seminole County, last staffed 1988 and still operational for emergencies; list and register positions differ.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab

events.note: Completed by the Georgia Forestry Commission, per the register
Last staffed in 1988, per the register
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: January 2, 2008

evidence.supports: Register: completed in 1952 by the Georgia Forestry Commission; 100-foot Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab; last staffed 1988; still operational for emergencies
evidence.quote: Completed in 1952 by the Georgia Forestry Commission, Seminole County Fire Tower is another late generation 100’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab. Last staffed in 1988, it is still operational for emergencies.

evidence.supports: Register: coordinates N 31.024510, W 084.879860, used for the 3.9 km comparison with the list position
List entry for seminole: Seminole County, coordinates 31.05622, -84.89646, elevation value 140

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The list gives 31.05622, -84.89646 and the register gives 31.02451, -84.87986 (N 31 01.471', W 84 52.792'). The two points are about 3.9 km apart by our calculation. The record keeps the list's position pending review; the story reports the difference.
The register gives 142 ft (43 m) and the list gives 140. The record's 42.7 m matches the list. The difference is small and both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Most facts rest on one register page (NHLR, cached crawl). One web search found no Georgia Forestry Commission or Donalsonville tower history; a search snippet about tower phase-out in the late 1980s was not read as a page and is not used. Height 30.5 m is 100 ft converted, not stated in the register in metres. Position differs by about 3.9 km between the list and the register, and the record keeps the list's position; check which is right before any map use. No source states public access, so no access key is set. Status 'standing' is from 'still operational for emergencies'.
